title: Observability Ceilings and Estimation Limits

blocks.md: This lesson covers the book's section on **Observability Ceilings and Estimation Limits**. Read the excerpt, then test yourself below.

blocks.source: Vol IV, Spatial Memory, § Observability Ceilings and Estimation Limits
blocks.md: A force sensor can report the exact same reading when mechanical contact force increases as when its analog conditioning circuit drifts thermally. Sampling that stream repeatedly cannot distinguish the two physical causes. The underlying question is observability, whether a system's available sensor outputs and known physical dynamics suffice to reconstruct the internal states required for control. Consider an instantaneous observation model MeasurementVector = ObservationFunction(EstimatorStateVector). When distinct physical states EstimatorStateVector_1 neq EstimatorStateVector_2 yield identical measurements (ObservationFunction(EstimatorStateVector_1) = ObservationFunction(EstimatorStateVector_2)), the sensor mapping alone cannot separate them.

blocks.prompt: Think first: In two or three sentences, explain why Observability ceiling matters for the system this section describes.
blocks.md: Compare your answer with the book's claim: When distinct state histories give identical measurements no estimator can separate them, and innovations stay near zero while the true state drifts, so observability must be designed in by excitation or added sensing.

questions.q: The section **Observability Ceilings and Estimation Limits** develops one of the chapter's claims. Which one?
options: When distinct state histories give identical measurements no estimator can separate them, and innovations stay near zero while the true state drifts, so observability must be designed in by excitation or added sensing.
A metric loop at camera rate keeps geometry current while foundation backbones update semantics on keyframes, and semantics never certify clearance.
Every spatial claim carries evidence, estimate, and publication epochs, and only a physical measurement advances the evidence epoch, so prediction and republishing must preserve it.
Tracking adds identity and velocity for planners, but a tentative track's occupied region must reach clearance consumers before confirmation and stays occupied while it coasts.
